resale_co.name: Residential Occupancy Certificate (ROC)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Roselle Division of Code Enforcement
resale_co.lead_time: Open construction permits must be finaled before the ROC inspection is scheduled; if no violations are found the certificate can be issued within 10 business days
resale_co.valid_for: Temporary certificate: up to 60 days (instructions page 1) or 90 days (checklist item 23)
requirements: 10-year sealed battery smoke detectors on all levels including basements and attics over 7 feet high, within 10 feet outside bedrooms; existing hardwired alarms kept
Carbon monoxide detectors in basements and within 10 feet outside bedrooms, plus inside any bedroom directly above a garage
2A10BC fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (1 and 2 family)
Bedroom windows open and close; windows and doors in good repair with proper hardware
Holes in walls, floors and ceilings repaired; missing tiles replaced and grouted
Hot and cold water with shut-off valves at kitchen and bath fixtures; toilets secure with shut-offs
GFI outlets within 6 feet of water and in all bathrooms; cover plates on all outlets, switches and junction boxes; dead wiring removed
Main electrical service line strapped to the building
Fireplaces and wood stoves with proper clearances and screens
Water heaters, boilers and furnaces working; relief valve discharge pipe within 4 inches of the floor; vents secured; gas shut-off in the same room
Sump pumps discharge outside, not into sanitary lines; garage door openers plugged directly into an outlet
Roofs, gutters and downspouts in good repair; handrails on stairs with 3 or more risers
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting and visible from the curb
Yard cut, trimmed and free of debris; all utilities on
All open construction permits finalized; work done without permits must get permits

fees.label: Temporary Residential Occupancy Certificate (at the inspector's discretion)
Each inspection beyond the second
fees.quote: Additional inspections over two (2) will be surcharged at $75.00 per inspection, (no exceptions.)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Residential Occupancy Certificate (Borough forms page, Local Code Enforcement) and return it with the fee to the Division of Code Enforcement, 210 Chestnut Street, Roselle. Company checks or money orders only; personal checks are not accepted. Confirm with the Building Department that all construction permits have final inspections, then schedule the ROC inspection. The buyer's name must be given before the certificate is issued.
resale_co.contact_title: Division of Code Enforcement (no ROC contact named; the application header lists (908) 259-3059)

resale_co.notes: The Borough's Residential Occupancy Certificate application asks for the buyer and says the buyer's name must be supplied before the certificate is issued, and the instructions say homes must have a final certificate for occupancy; the ordinance section requiring it on sale was not seen (Roselle's code is on ecode360). Fees for 3 family are $150.00 and 4 family $250.00. The instructions give a temporary certificate as valid up to 60 days while the checklist says 90 days; temporary certificates are only for bank-owned or uninhabitable homes being brought up to code. Code Enforcement officers listed on the Borough page: Valerie Watson (908-259-4509, vwatson@boroughofroselle.com), Walter Wimbush (908-259-3003, wwimbush@boroughofroselle.com), Rawle Jones (908-259-3032, jonesr@boroughofroselle.com); it does not say which one handles ROCs. Rentals: annual rental licensing ($50 per unit, Ordinance 2484-2014) and a Certificate of Use on each change of tenancy (Section 90-10); those are rental requirements.

requirements: The Borough ROC checklist covers 10-year sealed battery smoke alarms, CO alarms and a 2A10BC extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen; whether this replaces a separate fire certificate is not stated
